entries.principle_source: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct (2018), Section 2.5
entries.why_here: Rejects out-of-range or malformed applicant fields before inference so corrupted records cannot produce arbitrary scholarship screening outcomes.

entries.principle_source: ACM Code of Ethics and Professional Conduct (2018), Section 1.4
entries.why_here: Withholds `name` and `university` from the model prompt to eliminate the pair divergence observed in Part 1 on irrelevant identity and university-tier attributes.

entries.principle: Purpose Limitation, Consent, and Protection of Minors
entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Right to Privacy and Data Protection
entries.why_here: Blocks off-purpose requests, under-18 applicants, unconsented automated processing, and prompt-injection attempts in free-text fields before the model is called.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Responsibility and Accountability
entries.why_here: Records every screening and refusal event in `decisions.jsonl` with input hashes, withheld fields, raw outputs, and fired controls so decisions can be audited afterwards.

entries.principle_source: UNESCO Recommendation on the Ethics of Artificial Intelligence (2021), Human Oversight and Determination
entries.why_here: Routes borderline scores (45–60), unparseable outputs, decision-score contradictions, high-merit rejections, and bias-cue rationales to human reviewers.
